title: CLAUDE.md carries no repository profile, and three places cite one that is not there
summary: The shared operating block twice sends per-repository facts to 'each repository's own profile block below'; ci.yml cites "CLAUDE.md's repo profile - Ownership section" by name in a gating workflow; and docs/reference/lore-cli-repository-notes.md says the repo profile is one of the things that stayed in CLAUDE.md when reference material moved out. All three describe a section that does not exist. No CLAUDE.md in the rebuilt history (from e3d75867, the fresh-history cutover for the public repository) has ever carried one, so this is a restoration rather than a first draft. Two of ten fleet repositories are in this state and nothing detects it; opum-agent owns the fleet-level half. Consequence here: the per-repo ruleset facts, the promotion procedure ci.yml points at, and the promotion audit trap had nowhere to live, so they lived in session memory and were re-derived per session.

acceptanceCriteria.text: CLAUDE.md carries a repository profile using the fleet-canonical four headings, in order, with "None known." written out where a heading is empty
ci.yml cites a section that exists, and its Refuse the merge button error text names the remote-tracking promotion command rather than the stale-local-ref form
The audit trap is recorded: a promotion leaves no green run on the SHA that lands on main, and the only run there carries a designed red
Cross-repository reads are named concretely and verified by ref rather than recalled

implementationNotes:
WHY THIS WAS INVISIBLE, which is more useful than the omission itself. Three separate artifacts went on describing the profile after it stopped existing, and every one of them read as confirmation to anyone who checked:

  - the shared fleet block, twice, sending per-repository facts "to each repository's own profile block below"
  - .github/workflows/ci.yml, citing "CLAUDE.md's repo profile -- Ownership section" by name, in a GATING workflow
  - docs/reference/lore-cli-repository-notes.md, saying the repo profile is one of the things that STAYED in CLAUDE.md when reference material moved out under OPAG-37

All three were true before the fresh-history cutover (e3d75867) and false after it. A reader who checked the doc would conclude the profile was there. Nothing in the fleet compares prose to prose, which is the same family as OPAG-131.

VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, in the order it was checked:

  heading scan of CLAUDE.md          no profile, 75 lines, three sections and two managed blocks
  git log --all -- CLAUDE.md         the earliest rebuilt CLAUDE.md (e3d75867) has no profile either
  fleet survey (orchestrator, by ref) 7 of 10 repos carry the canonical four headings; quest-cli carries a
                                     nine-heading variant; lore-cli and opum-marketplace carry none
  lore-web CLAUDE.md, by ref         used as the compact reference implementation rather than opum-agent's,
                                     which carries orchestrator-only material

THE CROSS-REPO READ WAS MEASURED, NOT RECALLED. opum-marketplace's federated-pin-baselines.json read from its origin/main: opum-lore pinned at v0.7.0, skills/ subtree 2998f74d077845f8ad73f83aa296e37e034378a4. And the negative half, which is the part that usually goes unwritten: no sibling repository references a lore-cli/ file path by ref -- checked across opum-agent, opum-doc, opum-cli-e2e and opum-marketplace on their own dev. The coupling is the published artifact, not a path into this checkout.

TWO DEFECTS FIXED IN ci.yml BEYOND THE DANGLING CITATION. The "Refuse the merge button" error told the operator to run `git push origin dev:main` -- the stale-local-ref form. In a recycled session local dev can be behind, and that command fast-forwards main to the wrong SHA while still reporting success (ODOC-193). It now names origin/dev:main and says why. A guardrail whose error message hands out the wrong command is worse than no guardrail, because it is read at exactly the moment someone is being careful.

TIER 2 WAS FOLLOWED RATHER THAN ASSUMED SATISFIED. CLAUDE.md is a governing file, so a peer naming the fact did not authorise the edit. The orchestrator named it and explicitly declined to draft it; the user approved writing it and asked for fleet alignment first; the orchestrator supplied the template and the survey, not the prose. The wording here is this session's.
finalSummary:
CLAUDE.md now carries a repository profile, in the fleet-canonical four headings, and the three artifacts that were citing one restore to being true rather than needing edits of their own.

It is a restoration, not a first draft: no CLAUDE.md in the rebuilt history has ever carried one, and the section was lost in the fresh-history cutover for the public repository. What made that survive unnoticed for five days is that the shared fleet block, ci.yml, and this repo's own reference notes all went on describing it — three confirmations, none of them checked against the file.

The content is the material that had nowhere else to live and was therefore re-derived per session: the dev ruleset's five required contexts and the U+00B7 trap in two of them, main carrying no ruleset at all, the promotion shape ci.yml cites as procedure, release.yml being dispatch-only (which is what makes promotion here ordinary delivery rather than registry publication), and opum-marketplace's federation of skills/ by tag — read from their origin/main, together with the negative finding that no sibling reads a path into this checkout.

The headline entry is the promotion audit trap: CI does not run on dev pushes here, so a squash commit on dev never gets its own run, and the promotion PR's run is the ONLY run on the SHA that lands on main — a run that necessarily contains promotion is manual failing by design. An auditor looking for a green run on main's SHA finds a red one and concludes the promotion was unqualified. The gating evidence is on the dev-side PR head, and the profile says to cite that run by number.

Two defects were fixed in ci.yml on the way: a citation naming a section that did not exist, and a Refuse the merge button error message handing the operator `git push origin dev:main` — the stale-local-ref form that fast-forwards main to the wrong SHA while reporting success. A guardrail's error text is read at exactly the moment someone is being careful, so a wrong command there is worse than none.

What stays open is not here: two of ten repositories had no profile and nothing detects that, which is opum-agent's to file — prose that no check compares to anything, the same family as OPAG-131.
